\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Adjacency matrix word]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.adjWord}
\label{Randomized.Matching.adjWord}
\leanok
Given a Boolean matrix $A$ indexed by pairs of elements of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, form a
Boolean word by listing its entries row by row: first all entries in row $0$ in
increasing column order, then those in row $1$, and so on through row $n-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bipartite graph encoding]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.encodeBPM}
\label{Randomized.Matching.encodeBPM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Matching.adjWord, Turing.pairEncode}
Given a natural number $n$ and a Boolean matrix $A$ indexed by pairs of elements of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, encode the bipartite graph represented by $A$ as the pair encoding
of the length-$n$ word consisting entirely of true values and the row-by-row word of
entries of $A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Language of bipartite perfect matchings]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.BipartitePerfectMatching}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p018-b003,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p018-b004
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b005}
\label{Randomized.Matching.BipartitePerfectMatching}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Matching.HasPerfectMatching, Randomized.Matching.encodeBPM}
The language consists of exactly those Boolean strings $x$ for which there exist a
natural number $n$ and an $n\times n$ Boolean matrix $A$ such that $x$ is the encoding
of $A$ and the bipartite graph represented by $A$ has a perfect matching.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Adjacency matrix from a word]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.adjOfWord}
\label{Randomized.Matching.adjOfWord}
\leanok
Given a natural number $n$ and a Boolean word $w$, define an $n$-by-$n$ Boolean matrix
whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$ is the $(in+j)$-th entry of $w$, using false when
that position is outside the word.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Encoding membership and perfect matchings]

encoded pair consisting of a word of $n$ ones and the row-by-row list of entries of $A$

\begin{definition}[Randomized matching verifier]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.matchingVerifier}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p005-b005}
\label{Randomized.Matching.matchingVerifier}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.lovaszBits, Complexity.BinArith.lovaszPrime, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.Matching.adjOfWord, Randomized.Matching.encodeBPM, Randomized.Matching.lovaszMatrix, Randomized.Matching.lovaszSample}
Given Boolean strings $x$ and $r$, let $n$ be the length of the first component decoded
from $x$, and form the Boolean adjacency matrix of size $n$ from the second decoded
component. The verifier accepts exactly when $x$ is the prescribed encoding of that
matrix, the random string has length at least $n^2$ times the prescribed number of
sampling bits for $n$, and the determinant of the matrix obtained by applying the
prescribed Lovász construction to the matrix and the sample from $r$ is nonzero.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lovász entry word]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.lovaszEntryW}
\label{Randomized.Matching.lovaszEntryW}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
For a Boolean list $S$, define its Lovász entry word to be the binary expansion of the
natural number encoded by the second component of the second component of $S$ if the
first component of the second component of $S$ has first bit true; otherwise, define it
to be the empty list. Missing first bits are treated as false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lovász row word]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.lovaszRowW}
\label{Randomized.Matching.lovaszRowW}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.chunkW, Complexity.BinArith.zipWithW, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.Matching.lovaszEntryW, Turing.pairEncode}
For a Boolean list $S$, form the pair encoding of the empty list with the pair encoding
of two words: the chunk of the pair encoding of the one-bit word $[\mathrm{true}]$ and
the first component of the second component of $S$, and the chunk of the pair encoding
of the first component of $S$ and the second component of the second component of $S$.
Apply the width-indexed zip operation with the Lovász entry-word function to this
encoded list.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lovász row array]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.lovaszRows}
\label{Randomized.Matching.lovaszRows}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and Boolean lists $w$ and $r$, define an $n$-by-$n$
array of natural numbers whose $(i,j)$ entry, for $0\le i,j<n$, is the natural number
encoded by the length-$k$ block of $r$ starting at position $(ni+j)k$ if the bit of $w$
at position $ni+j$ is true, and is zero otherwise. Missing bits of $w$ are treated as
false, and the block is truncated if $r$ ends before its full length.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Encoded Lovász Sample Matrix]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.zipWithW_lovaszRowW}
\label{Randomized.Matching.zipWithW_lovaszRowW}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.chunkList, Complexity.BinArith.chunkW, Complexity.BinArith.chunkW_pairEncode, Complexity.BinArith.decWords_encWords, Complexity.BinArith.encMat, Complexity.BinArith.encRow, Complexity.BinArith.encWords, Complexity.BinArith.zipWithW, Complexity.BinArith.zipWithW_pairEncode, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Randomized.Matching.lovaszEntryW, Randomized.Matching.lovaszRowW, Randomized.Matching.lovaszRows, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $K,u,w,NK,r$ be finite bit strings. Suppose $w$ has length $|u|^2$, $NK$ has length
$|u||K|$, $r$ has length $|u||NK|$, and either $K$ is nonempty or $u$ is empty. Then
applying the encoded row procedure to $K$, the chunked adjacency word from $u,w$, and
the chunked sample word from $NK,r$ yields the encoding of the matrix with $|u|$ rows
and columns whose $(i,j)$ entry is the binary value of the length-$|K|$ block of $r$
beginning at position $(|u|i+j)|K|$ if the bit of $w$ at position $|u|i+j$ is true, and
is zero otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rows encoding the sampled adjacency matrix]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.matOfRows_lovaszRows}
\label{Randomized.Matching.matOfRows_lovaszRows}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.matOfRows, Randomized.Matching.adjOfWord, Randomized.Matching.lovaszMatrix, Randomized.Matching.lovaszRows, Randomized.Matching.lovaszSample, Randomized.blockVal}
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $n,p,k$ and bit strings $w,r$, form an $n\times n$ Boolean matrix by
reading the bit of $w$ at position $in+j$ for entry $(i,j)$. From $r$, take the block of
$k$ bits beginning at position $(in+j)k$ for each entry, interpret it as a natural
number, and reduce modulo $p$. The matrix over the integers modulo $p$ whose entries are
these reduced block values when the corresponding Boolean entry is $1$, and zero
otherwise, equals the resulting masked sample matrix.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Derived key word]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.tK}
\label{Randomized.Matching.tK}

\begin{definition}[Encoded product word]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.tNK}
\label{Randomized.Matching.tNK}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.mulU, Randomized.Matching.tK, Randomized.Matching.tU, Turing.pairEncode}
For a Boolean list $z$, pair-encode $t_U(z)$ and $t_K(z)$ and apply the unary
multiplication encoding to that pair; the resulting list is $t_{NK}(z)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coin prefix]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.tCoins}
\label{Randomized.Matching.tCoins}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.mulU, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.Matching.tNK, Randomized.Matching.tU, Randomized.takePrefixByLen, Turing.pairEncode}
For a Boolean list $z$, form the pair encoding of the unary multiplication encoding of
the pair encoding of $t_U(z)$ and $t_{NK}(z)$, together with the second component of the
defaulted pair decoding of $z$. Define $t_{\mathrm{Coins}}(z)$ to be the prefix of $z$
whose length is specified by that encoded pair.
\end{definition}

For a Boolean list $z$, define its determinant-based output string by applying the

\begin{definition}[Matching certificate test]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.matchingTest}

For a Boolean string $z$, return true exactly when all four conditions hold: the
prescribed width-aware encoding equality holds for the first component of $z$, the
product encoding built from its two decoded parameters has length equal to the decoded
witness length, the product encoding built from the first parameter and the decoded
parameter $tNK$ has length at most the second decoded component's length, and the
integer represented by the decoded determinant component is nonzero.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of valid graph encodings]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.eq_encodeBPM_iff}

\difficulty{4}
For every bit string $x$, let $u$ and $v$ be the first and second components returned by
parsing $x$ as a self-delimiting pair, using the empty word for a component when parsing
fails. Then $x$ equals the encoding formed from a word of $|u|$ ones and the adjacency
matrix decoded from $v$ (with missing matrix entries read as false) if and only if $x$
is the pair encoding of a word of $|u|$ ones and $v$, and $|u|^2=|v|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bipartite matching is in RP]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.inRP_BipartitePerfectMatching}
\label{Randomized.Matching.inRP_BipartitePerfectMatching}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.lovaszBits, Complexity.BinArith.lovaszBits_le, Complexity.BinArith.lovaszPrime, Complexity.BinArith.lovaszPrime_prime, Complexity.BinArith.two_mul_le_two_pow_lovaszBits, Complexity.BinArith.two_pow_lt_lovaszPrime, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Randomized.InRP, Randomized.Matching.BipartitePerfectMatching, Randomized.Matching.HasPerfectMatching, Randomized.Matching.adjOfWord, Randomized.Matching.det_lovaszMatrix_eq_zero, Randomized.Matching.eff_matchingVerifier, Randomized.Matching.encodeBPM, Randomized.Matching.length_adjWord, Randomized.Matching.lovaszMatrix, Randomized.Matching.lovaszSample, Randomized.Matching.lovasz_test_zmod, Randomized.Matching.matchingVerifier, Randomized.Matching.matchingVerifier_encodeBPM, Randomized.inRPWeak_iff_inRP, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.polyTimeModel_closedUnderAny, Randomized.randProb_congr, Turing.length_pairEncode}

The language of encodings of bipartite graphs that have a perfect matching belongs to RP
under the given verifier model. Explicitly, there are a Boolean verifier $M$ and natural
numbers $a,k$ such that the verifier is efficient according to that model, every input
word in the language is accepted with probability at least $2/3$ using $a(|x|+1)^k$

choice of those random bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bipartite matching is in BPP]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.inBPP_BipartitePerfectMatching}
\label{Randomized.Matching.inBPP_BipartitePerfectMatching}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
The language of encodings of bipartite graphs that have a perfect matching belongs to
BPP under the given verifier model. Explicitly, there are a Boolean verifier $M$ and
natural numbers $a,k$ such that the verifier is efficient according to that model, and
for every input word $x$, if $x$ is in the language then a uniformly random string of
$a(|x|+1)^k$ bits makes $M$ accept with probability at least $2/3$; if $x$ is not in the
language, such a random string makes $M$ reject with probability at least $2/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Perfect matching in one-sided polynomial time]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.BipartitePerfectMatching_mem_RP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.Matching.BipartitePerfectMatching_mem_RP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.Matching.BipartitePerfectMatching, Randomized.Matching.inRP_BipartitePerfectMatching, Randomized.RP_PTM, Randomized.mem_RP_PTM_iff}
\difficulty{1}
The language of encodings of Boolean adjacency matrices whose associated bipartite graph
has a perfect matching is decidable by a probabilistic Turing machine in polynomial
time, accepting each member with probability at least $2/3$ and rejecting each nonmember
on every computation branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Perfect matching in bounded-error polynomial time]
\lean{Randomized.Matching.BipartitePerfectMatching_mem_BPP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.Matching.BipartitePerfectMatching_mem_BPP_PTM}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
The language of encodings of Boolean adjacency matrices whose associated bipartite graph
has a perfect matching is decidable by a probabilistic Turing machine in polynomial
time, with acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members and at most $1/3$ on
nonmembers.
\end{theorem}
